title:
Epics are functions that dispatch actions as a result of other actions being triggered. You can think of
them as subscription handlers for component actions.

You should use them whenever you need a component's action to have an effect on itself or other components.
For example you might want to open a modal when a button is clicked or validate the input of a field when the
user stops typing, in such cases you can write an epic function that "listens" to actions and returns the
corresponding actions you want executed as a result.

There are two types of epics you can use depending on how complex the logic driving the side effects is:

1. UiSdlEpic. Whenever there's a need to delay, orchestrate or throttle actions, you should implement your own `UiSdlEpic` type
and override `epic`. Another way to see them is as an asynchronous many-to-many side effect.
2. {@link UiSdlSimpleEpic}. When your logic is synchronous and you can map a single action to a collection of actions,
implement a `UiSdlSimpleEpic` type and override `simpleEpic`. You can think of them as a synchronous one-to-many side effect.

For more information about implementing epics, refer to [Communication between components](communication-between-component.c3doc.md)
@see https://redux-observable.js.org/docs/basics/Epics.html
